title: Unity: The We Is the Shared Me
coreMove: Distinguish real shared identity from borrowed belonging cues before letting scrutiny drop.
sourcePressure: The source supports unity as the added 2021 principle: shared identity, belonging, we-ness, common fate, boundary softening, and the distinction from liking or similarity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not flatten unity into liking; unity works when the other side feels like part of us, not merely pleasant or similar.

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer deciding whether to skip inventory checks for a fellow member
exampleSpecs.stakes: letting we-ness override accountability during flood recovery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the volunteer hears our people take care of our people, then still counts the medical kits before release
exampleSpecs.firstImage: plastic bins of bandages stacked on a church gym floor

exampleSpecs.audience: a parent asked to underwrite a curriculum purchase
exampleSpecs.stakes: approving a weak vendor because the pitch invokes shared ancestry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent honors the shared heritage line, then asks for the vendor comparison matrix before pledging
exampleSpecs.firstImage: handwritten alphabet cards taped along a hallway

exampleSpecs.audience: a member-owner hearing a supplier claim cooperative values
exampleSpecs.stakes: buying a mixer because the supplier borrows co-op language
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the member asks how the warranty and service terms reflect shared risk rather than just shared words
exampleSpecs.firstImage: flour dust on a meeting packet beside a dough hook

exampleSpecs.audience: siblings asked to join a cousin's land fund
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusing family identity with investment diligence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the family call, one sibling marks which claims were kinship appeals and which were verifiable documents
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a video-call grid reflected in a dark kitchen window

exampleSpecs.audience: a maintainer asked to trust a longtime contributor's release shortcut
exampleSpecs.stakes: shipping insecure code because we built this together feels binding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the maintainer contrasts the contributor's history with the failed security checklist and keeps the review requirement
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a terminal window showing a failed dependency scan

exampleSpecs.audience: a graduate considering a business loan from an alumni lender
exampleSpecs.stakes: accepting poor terms because school identity feels like protection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the graduate circles every alumni phrase in the pitch, then compares interest, collateral, and penalties to two non-alumni lenders
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a loan folder embossed with the old campus seal

skillTargets: distinguish unity from liking and similarity
preserve scrutiny inside real shared identity
evaluate when common fate is substantive versus rhetorical

tryThisNowSpec: When a request uses we language today, write what is actually shared, what is only being claimed, and what evidence should still be checked.
